value.title: Docs in the pij CLI: refusals and first turns point at pages
value.summary: PRD 009 workstream step s04 (req-06). The seat-type refusals end with the `pij docs` page that explains them, and a seat started in a role is told its type's page instead of the type's whole definition. The page ids come from one place in the type catalog, which `pij docs` also uses.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: PRD 006's refusals (`E-RS-TYPE-MISSING`, `-UNKNOWN`, `-FIELD`, `-RULE`) list the ten types or name a flag, and PRD 007's first turn carried each type's purpose, lifecycle, keeps and every rule. Both now point at the page: a refusal's message ends `Read: pij docs get types` (or `types/<type>`), with its code and runnable next step unchanged, and the first turn's type part becomes the type's line, its authority, `Your type in full: pij docs get types/<type>`, only the rules the role changes (with their reasons, which no page holds) and the seed. That changes what every new seat is told: across the ten shipped types the type part shrinks from 9,737 to 6,220 characters (36%, mean 973 to 622), measured with the format strings before and after on the shipped definitions and seeds, with no rule changes. `types::DOCS_PAGE` and `types::docs_page()` name the pages for both the refusals and `pij docs`, so they cannot drift apart.

sections.name: goals
value: A seat refused for a type, or started in a role, is pointed at the page that explains its type.
A first turn carries what only it can: the role's own rule changes, the seed, the role and its memory.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Changing any refusal's code, next step or when it fires.
The pods page (req-05): PRD 008's pod commands are not on main.
Pointers in refusals that do not turn on a type.

value.claim: `E-RS-TYPE-MISSING` and `E-RS-TYPE-UNKNOWN` messages end `Read: pij docs get types`; `E-RS-TYPE-FIELD` and every `E-RS-TYPE-RULE` end `Read: pij docs get types/<type>`. Codes and `next` are unchanged.

A first turn's type part is `You are a <type> seat (<title>): <line>`, `Carries authority: yes|no.`, `Your type in full: pij docs get types/<type>`, then `Your role changes these rules of your type:` with each changed rule's text, id and reason (only when the role changes one), then the seed. It no longer carries the type's purpose, lifecycle, keeps or unchanged rules.

The type pages say a seat started in a role gets the seed and a pointer to the page; building-a-role and concepts describe `pij-rs spawn --as role:<id>`, `pij directory show <role> --first-turn` and `pij close --stop`, which PRD 007 shipped, instead of calling them planned.

value.title: Pointers shipped
value.brief: One PR: refusal messages, the first turn's type part, the pages that described PRD 007 as planned.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Refusals: `check_role_for` and `get` in `crates/daemon/src/community/types.rs` (a `Refusal` is a code, a message and one runnable `next`; the pointer goes in the message so `next` stays the one command to run). First turn: the type part of `assemble` in `crates/daemon/src/community/first_turn.rs` (PRD 007, plan 242); `reshape_http/role_start.rs` asserts the role, parameters and creator parts, not the type part.

value.risk: A seat that cannot run `pij docs` (no pij on its PATH) loses its type's definition from its first turn.
value.mitigation: Every seat pij starts runs beside pij; the line, authority, the role's changes and the seed stay in the first turn, and `pij directory types <type>` prints the same definition.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: no loop, poll, timer, hook or launch. A refusal formats one more sentence; the first turn formats less. Nothing per seat or per tick.
Pages and messages are public-safe: no customer or person names.
